questions.question: Look at this increasing pattern: 5, 9, 13, 17, ___ . What is the next number?
questions.explain: Find the constant change first: 9 − 5 = 4, so the rule is add 4 each time, and 17 + 4 = 21. A common trap is guessing a change of 2 (19) without checking the gap between every pair of numbers.

questions.question: A decreasing pattern goes 40, 36, 32, 28, … Which sentence describes the pattern rule?
options: Start at 40 and subtract 4 each time
Start at 40 and subtract 2 each time
Start at 40 and add 4 each time
Start at 28 and subtract 4 each time
questions.explain: A pattern rule needs both the starting number and the change: it starts at 40 and 40 − 36 = 4, so you subtract 4 each time. A common trap is naming the change correctly but starting from the last number you see instead of the first.

questions.question: What is the value of the expression 2n + 5 when n = 6?
questions.explain: Multiply before you add: 2 × 6 = 12, then 12 + 5 = 17. Two common traps are stopping at 12 (forgetting the + 5) and adding first to get 2 × 11 = 22.

questions.question:
This table shows a pattern.
Term number (t): 1, 2, 3, 4
Value: 4, 8, 12, 16
Which expression describes the pattern?
questions.explain: Test an expression on every row, not just the first: 4t gives 4, 8, 12, 16 for t = 1, 2, 3, 4. The trap is picking t + 3 because it works for the first term only — at t = 2 it gives 5, not 8.

questions.question: Priya puts $7 in her jar in Week 1, then adds $5 every week after that. How much money is in her jar in Week 6?
questions.explain: From Week 1 to Week 6 she adds money 5 times, so 7 + (5 × $5) = $32. The most common trap is adding $5 six times to get $37 — Week 1 already happened before any $5 was added.

questions.question: Owen builds a growing pattern with colour tiles. Figure 1 uses 5 tiles, Figure 2 uses 8 tiles, and Figure 3 uses 11 tiles. Which expression tells how many tiles Figure n uses?
questions.explain: The tiles go up by 3 each figure, so start with 3n, then check Figure 1: 3 × 1 = 3, which is 2 short of 5, giving 3n + 2. The trap is writing only 3n and forgetting the 2 tiles that are there in every figure.

questions.question: A class graphed the number of fluent speakers of a First Peoples language: 2015 → 96 speakers, 2016 → 88, 2017 → 80, 2018 → 72. If this decreasing pattern keeps going, how many fluent speakers would there be in 2020?
questions.explain: The number drops by 8 each year, and 2020 is 2 years after 2018, so 72 − 8 − 8 = 56. The common trap is subtracting only once (64) instead of counting how many years pass.

questions.question: In a school gym, tables are set up in a pattern where Figure n has 2n + 1 chairs. Which figure has exactly 25 chairs?
questions.explain: Work backwards through the expression: 25 − 1 = 24, then 24 ÷ 2 = 12, so it is Figure 12. The trap is subtracting the 1 but forgetting to divide by 2 (24), or dividing 25 by 2 and rounding up to 13.

questions.question: Noah and Ava track their money each week. In Week 1 Noah has $5 and he saves $4 more every week. In Week 1 Ava has $29 and she spends $2 every week. In which week do they have the same amount of money?
questions.explain: Build both patterns side by side in a table: Noah has 5, 9, 13, 17, 21 and Ava has 29, 27, 25, 23, 21, so they match in Week 5 at $21. The trap is comparing only one pattern or stopping as soon as the numbers look close instead of continuing until they are equal.

questions.question: Sam looks at the pattern 3, 5, 7, 9, … and says, "It goes up by 2, so the expression is 2n." Which choice gives the correct expression and the correct 20th term?
questions.explain: The change of 2 gives the 2n part, but 2 × 1 = 2 and the first term is 3, so you must add 1: the expression is 2n + 1 and the 20th term is 2 × 20 + 1 = 41. The most common mistake is using only the difference (2n) and forgetting the constant that lines the expression up with the first term.

questions.question: Before a language program started, the number of young speakers of a First Peoples language fell by 6 each year: 2018 → 54, 2019 → 48, 2020 → 42. The program began in 2020, and after that the number rose by 9 each year. How many young speakers would there be in 2024?
questions.explain: Start from the 2020 value of 42 and add 9 once for each of the 4 years to 2024: 51, 60, 69, 78. The trap is either keeping the old decreasing rule going or miscounting the years — 2020 to 2024 is 4 increases, not 3 or 5.

questions.question: Marcus graphs a colour-tile pattern. The points are (1, 6), (2, 10), (3, 14), and (4, 18), where x is the figure number and y is the number of tiles. Which statement is correct?
options: The expression is 6n, so Figure 9 uses 54 tiles
The expression is n + 4, so Figure 9 uses 13 tiles
The expression is 4n, so Figure 9 uses 36 tiles
The expression is 4n + 2, so Figure 9 uses 38 tiles
questions.explain: The y-values rise by 4 for each step in x, so the expression starts as 4n, and since 4 × 1 = 4 while Figure 1 has 6 tiles, the rule is 4n + 2, giving 4 × 9 + 2 = 38. The trap is using the first point as a multiplier (6n) or using only the difference (4n) without checking it against a point on the graph.
